title: Pairwise detection, chiral conversion: Resource theory of quantum multistates
authors: Yuan-Hong Tao, Yu-Xin Wu, Bing Xie, Lin Zhang
abstract: Basis-independent coherence of a quantum multistate is fixed by whether its constituent states commute, and for qubits it is detected by pairwise state overlaps alone. What governs its deterministic transformation has been open. We give the exact resource-conversion theory of quantum multistates under common commutativity-preserving operations (CPOs). For qubits, pairwise Bargmann invariants determine the singular values of the unique candidate channel, while a single third-order Bargmann phase determines its orientation. Complete positivity then yields a necessary and sufficient criterion for exact conversion. The criterion identifies a chirality-sensitive shell $\mathcal C_{\rm chir}$, within which targets with identical pairwise geometry can differ in convertibility solely by the sign of their cubic invariant. This yields an order separation, $k_{\rm detect}=2<3=k_{\rm convert}$, for qubit multistates of every size $n\geqslant3$. The chirality-sensitive shell occupies exactly one third of the singular-value simplex, while mirror reflection obstructs two thirds of the admissible orientation-preserving transformations by volume. For $d\geqslant3$, by contrast, the structure is rigid: every resourceful conversion is realized by either an isotropic depolarizing or a transpose-depolarizing channel. Convertibility is then decided by centered Bargmann invariants of degree at most $d^2$.
summary: This paper develops a resource-conversion theory for quantum multistates, showing that while pairwise overlaps (second-order invariants) are sufficient for detection, exact transformation requires higher-order invariants (third-order invariants) due to chirality. The analysis rigorously defines the necessary and sufficient conditions for such conversions, revealing structural rigidity in higher dimensions.
main_problem: The paper determines the exact resource-conversion theory for quantum multistates under common commutativity-preserving operations (CPOs). It investigates whether pairwise state overlaps are sufficient to govern the deterministic transformation between coherent ensembles.
main_result: For qubits, detectability relies on second-order invariants, but exact conversion requires third-order invariants, establishing an order separation ($k_{	ext{detect}}=2 < k_{	ext{convert}}=3$). Furthermore, the structure is rigid for higher dimensions ($d \ge 3$).
method: The authors use resource theory concepts, analyzing the complete positivity (CP) of the candidate transformation channel ($\Phi_T$) derived from pairwise overlaps. They employ Bargmann invariants ($\Delta_k$) to characterize the state geometry and the transformation's orientation (chirality).
model_or_system: The system under study is a quantum multistate $ho = (ho_1, \dots, ho_n)$ in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, with a specific focus on qubits ($d=2$). The transformations are constrained to Common Commutativity-Preserving Operations (CPOs).
key_observables: Pairwise overlaps (second-order Bargmann invariants, $\Delta_2$), third-order Bargmann invariants ($\Delta_3$), singular values of the transformation matrix $T$, and the chirality sign $\eta$.
important_parameters: The dimensionality $d$ (especially $d=2$ vs $d \ge 3$), the number of states $n$, and the degree of the invariant ($k=2$ vs $k=3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a candidate channel $\Phi_T$ fixed by the ratio of Bloch matrices ($T = S R^{-1}$) and relies on the definition of CPOs.
figures_summary: Figure 1 contrasts detection (using $\Delta_2$) versus conversion (requiring $\Delta_3$). Figure 2 illustrates the singular-value simplex, partitioning it into regions (I, II, $\mathcal{C}_{	ext{chir}}$) based on CP conditions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the resource-conversion theory by first analyzing the qubit case ($d=2$), demonstrating the necessity of third-order invariants due to chirality. It then generalizes to higher dimensions ($d \ge 3$), showing a rigid structure governed by lower-degree invariants.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical constraints on how quantum correlations (coherence) can be transformed, linking fundamental algebraic invariants (Bargmann invariants) directly to operational feasibility (complete positivity) in resource theory.

FIG. 4: The dimensional anomaly. (a) For d = 2, a unital CPO is any point of the Pauli tetrahedron, so the Bloch ball may be deformed along three independent semi-axes. The isotropic axis λ1 = λ2 = λ3 = q is one line inside that body, q ∈[−1/3, 1]. The red dot marks a generic anisotropic channel. (b) For d ⩾3, CPOs with non-commutative range have a single scaling parameter q. The plot shows the admissible intervals [−1/(d2 −1), 1] for the unitary branch and [−1/(d −1), 1/(d + 1)] for the transpose branch. The latter has width 2d/(d2 −1) and shrinks toward q = 0 as d grows. At q = 0, the channel is completely depolarizing and has commutative range.
